_key_note: Ticket ids are KEY-001, KEY-002 and so on, issued in order and never reused. Ken takes the key from the ticket files already in tickets/, or from the workspace's initials when there are none, so this line is a record for people.
_repos_note: The sources this knowledge base covers. Ken keeps each repo's kind in its own registry on the machine, so kind here is a record: wiki, code or reference, and documents once Ken has that kind (ruled, not yet in Ken). base: the branch drift measures as origin/<base>; without one, drift uses the remote's default branch. Any repo may carry aliases, the short names pages already cite it by, its own ignore list, and roles, a path pattern to a role that Ken proposes when a code repo is added and writes here once a person accepts. A reference repo carries pin, the commit set-up read, and upstream, its origin; Ken will say when upstream moves past the pin (ruled, not yet in Ken). Set-up writes one entry for each repo the workspace covers.
_ignore_note: The index rules: one gitignore-style pattern a line, and a ! line brings a path back. They hold for every source, and a repos entry may carry its own. Built in and fixed: VCS folders, dependencies, build output, secrets, tests, minified and generated files, binaries. Three states will replace in or out: ignored, searchable only, and read by the AI, with big checkouts and code starting as searchable only (ruled, not yet in Ken).
_controls_note: A few known questions per source, each with the file it has to return near the top: { "question": "how are worlds saved", "expect": "src/world/save.ts", "source": "Game" }. Ken proposes them when a source is added and writes them here once a person accepts. They run after every rebuild and count on the health line.
_search_note: search.weights: a path pattern to a tier, by name: binding, current, reference, record or superseded. The longest pattern wins.
_drift_note: Drift runs when a cited repo's fetched branch moves, weekly, hourly while pages are waiting, and on Run drift now. All optional: controlMoved, a page known to have moved since its check, and controlClean, a page known to be clean, void a run that reads them wrong; minPages voids a run that examines fewer pages; fetch: false measures against the remote branches as last fetched. A run without controls is marked uncontrolled.
